note: Rewritten from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English, the genus lacks a soldier caste, and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens, distribution records and the account of the multivariate analysis are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species is based on a single colony series and was initially included in A. empodius. It differs from the latter in the proportions of the mandibles, especially the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible, and in the smaller ocellus of the alate, which is farther from the compound eye; the meso- and metanotum are wider at the constriction. The worker gut is shorter, and the enteric valve seating is nearly ventral and necked, whereas in A. empodius it is dorsolateral and almost sessile, and the third apical spur of the fore tibia is also very small. The additional ratio Oi.Ow/La.Ra is 0.66–0.72, against 1.25–1.85 in A. empodius. Within the group, the alates of A. ignavus and A. murcus have very long head setae, a shorter postclypeus and an ocellus closer to the compound eye, while the workers have a narrower fore tibia, a reduced third apical spur and a bilobate enteric valve seating.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white; pilosity pale yellow, very sparse and fine. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27, Pcl/Ri 3.08. Apical tooth of the mandibles moderately long, La/Li 0.75, Ra/Ri 1.08; the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 14.95; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible lie approximately on the same line, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth equal in length, composite ratio 19.10. Fore tibia almost not inflated, Ti/Ty 4.52; third apical spur distinct but smaller than the other two. Mesenteron-proctodeum junction almost transverse, lying to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating ventral in the unopened abdomen, markedly trilobate, the third lobe almost as large as the two outer lobes, connected to the second proctodeal pouch by a neck of moderate length; the membranous wall of the valve bears sparse microspines outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep sepia brown, slightly darker above the ocellus. Fontanelle distinct, pale brown to brown, broadly elliptical or subcircular, markedly depressed and roughened by irregular transverse ridges, only slightly smaller than the ocellus; central spot elliptical, brown to sepia brown, flat, slightly smaller than the fontanelle; postclypeus sepia brown, labrum pale yellowish brown; frontal spot distinct, semicircular, slightly concave to markedly depressed, sepia brown; antennae brown. Pronotum sepia brown, meso- and metanotum brown, both with dark transverse sutures; femora brown, tibiae pale brown, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles sepia brown, sternites brown with the middle very pale, ventral spiracles brown; cerci pale brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded; ocellus rather small, separated from the compound eye by up to one and one-third times its own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.25–0.26, Pcl/Ra 2.71–2.75, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of the mandibles rather short, L/L 0.65–0.66, Ra/Rj 0.89–0.91; subsidiary tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 7.47–8.83; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible lie on the same line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of the second. Head pilosity pale brown, uneven, not felt-like. Constriction of the meso- and metanotum slightly wide, M/W 0.27–0.32. Third apical spur of the fore tibia distinct.
